newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Health Ministry OKs deposit rate cut - paper.
newsitem.headline: Japan Health Ministry OKs deposit rate cut - paper.

text.p: Japan's Health and Welfare Ministry has agreed to a cut in the rate on its deposits at the Ministry of Finance's (MOF) Trust Fund Bureau early next week by 0.1 percentage point to 2.8 percent, the financial daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said on Friday.
Health Minister Junichiro Koizumi had refused to accept a cut in the deposit rate, which the Finance Ministry had sought following recent falls in the issue rate of 10-year Japanese government bonds.
The deposit rate, which has been unchanged since January, is customarily set based on the bond issue rate.
Koizumi and Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka discussed the matter on Friday evening, the paper said.
Koizumi has called for changes in the governments' Fiscal Investment and Loan Programme (FILP), which is managed by the Trust Fund Bureau.

The bureau channels massive funds raised via deposits made by the Health and Posts and Telecommunications ministries to government-affiliated financial institutions and other quasi-government bodies for the FILP.
